subject: Post-call MAP: Legal redlines & negotiation ownership
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T15:06:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + MAP (legal milestone & next steps)

Thanks again for a productive call this morning, Samantha — good to align on usage patterns and success criteria. As promised, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on milestones, owners, and target close window. I pulled out the legal negotiation milestone as its own line item since both teams flagged MSA/DPA/SLA redlines as a critical path.

Quick highlights and asks from our side:
- Target close: end of calendar November (11/30) — flexible if legal needs more time but want to capture a committed window in the MAP.
- Legal milestone (proposed): Acme to provide initial MSA/DPA redlines by 11/05; Redwood to respond with counter-redlines within 3 business days. Final signoff target: 11/20.
- Ownership: proposed split — Acme legal owns initial redline submission (we'll accept tracked changes), Redwood legal (cc: Rishi) will own the counter with suggested fallback language for SLA and data residency clauses.
- Turnaround SLAs: 3 business days for substantive redline review during initial exchange; 5 business days thereafter for any new commercial terms.
- Dependencies: procurement budget approval (Tom Lee), SOC2 evidence pack (we shared last call), and an agreed list of production IP/data flow diagrams.

Attached: 20261028-Acme-MAP-Draft-v1.xlsx (MAP table) — please review columns for "Legal owner", "Requested due", and "Dependencies".

Next steps (from call):
1) Samantha: confirm Acme legal point-of-contact + expected redline date (prefer by 11/05).
2) Tom: confirm procurement timing and whether a PO or contract signature is the gating artifact.
3) Redwood: we'll prepare a suggested counter-redline template and an SLA fallback paragraph for quick negotiation.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute follow-up if that helps accelerate alignment.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

Ben — thanks for the summary and the MAP. Quick clarifications from our side: we can aim to share initial redlines by 11/05, but that depends on one thing — confirmation from procurement on whether we need to route via our central contracting team (likely) or can sign an operating agreement locally.

Legal contact: I've looped in legal@acmehealth.com (internal intake address) — lead counsel will be Priya Rao (priya.rao@acmehealth.com). Priya will confirm if they want tracked changes or a clean marked-up draft; I'll ask for tracked changes to speed review.

On your proposed turnaround: 3 business days to review a first counter seems aggressive for our legal team when they also have other enterprise negotiations. Can we compromise to 5 business days for Redwood to return counter-redlines on week 1, and 3 business days for targeted responses only on critical SLA clauses thereafter? That would make the 11/20 signoff target tight but potentially feasible.

I'll also confirm procurement timing with Tom and update the MAP spreadsheet.

Thanks —
Sam

Thanks Sam — appreciate the fast reply and the legal contact. Based on your note, here's an updated, concrete proposal for the MAP legal milestone that I included in the attached redlines doc (Acme_MSA_Redlines_20261101.docx):

- Initial submission (Acme): by 2026-11-05 — Acme legal to submit redlines in tracked changes to the attached MSA draft.
- Redwood initial counter: within 5 business days of receipt (we can commit to this given our legal availability); if redlines are limited to SLA and data residency, Redwood will prioritize and return an initial targeted counter within 3 business days for those clauses.
- Escalation path: if either party has unresolved material commercial terms after two full exchange cycles, escalation goes to Ben Carter (sales lead) and Priya Rao (Acme counsel) for a 24-48 hour decision window.
- Final signoff target: 2026-11-20 (soft target) — dependent on procurement confirmation.
- Ownership notes: Acme owns initial redlines and procurement gating; Redwood owns preparing the counter-template and SLA fallback language. We will not introduce new commercial terms after our first counter unless explicitly requested by Acme.

Lauren & Grace — can you confirm Redwood legal will accept tracked changes and that the 5-business-day initial counter SLA is realistic? Rishi — can you confirm your team will prioritize SLA/data-residency items when flagged as critical?

If that looks okay, I'll update the MAP spreadsheet and set the milestone owner fields accordingly. We can also add a short mutual agreement line: "Both parties agree to reasonably cooperate to respond to redlines within the timelines above; exceptions to be documented in writing."

Best,
Ben Carter
